name: High-Flow PLA (High-Speed PLA)
chemical_makeup: Base polylactide reformulated for a high melt-flow index (lower melt viscosity) and dosed with nucleating agents that accelerate crystallisation immediately after extrusion; no filler, no co-polymer blend
summary: Base PLA rheology-tuned for speed — same lactide chemistry, process delta only. Versus base PLA the melt is thinner and re-solidifies faster, lifting the usable speed band from roughly 40-100 mm/s to 100-300 mm/s (600+ mm/s on capable hardware) and volumetric flow from ~24 to ~28 mm³/s on Prusa's own comparison. Nozzle and bed temperatures are near-identical to base PLA and near-100 % part cooling becomes mandatory rather than merely advisable. Strength, heat resistance and weather behaviour are unchanged; the finish is glossier and less forgiving of defects than matte PLA.

printing.notes: Delta vs base PLA: temperatures barely move (Polymaker PolySonic PLA Pro 210-230 °C, Prusament PLA High Speed tuned around 220 °C at high flow, eSUN ePLA-HS ~220 °C; eSUN's tested bed range is 30-45 °C), but speed does — PolySonic PLA Pro is rated 100-300 mm/s and the class is commonly run at 250-600 mm/s on high-flow hotends, against 40-100 mm/s for typical PLA profiles. Prusa measures 28 mm³/s at 220 °C for PLA High Speed against 24 mm³/s for standard Prusament PLA. Full-power part cooling is not optional here: the nucleated melt has to be frozen quickly to hold shape at speed, so the fan effectively lives at 100 %. That makes an open frame preferable and an enclosed machine should be run with the door/lid open, as with base PLA. Unfilled, so no hardened nozzle.

feeding.notes: Feeds exactly like base PLA — rigid, unfilled, non-abrasive, no PTFE wear concern, no spool-side assistant needed, and Bambu's material guidance flags no high-speed PLA as barred from the AMS. Rated 'yes' like base PLA rather than the 'conditional' carried by pla-cf and lw-pla. No shore hardness applies (rigid grade).

drying.dryness_validation: No popping/crackling or steam at the nozzle and no foamy extrudate — worth checking at the intended print speed, since moisture artefacts that a slow profile hides show up as rough walls at 250+ mm/s. Minimal stringing on a retraction test.
drying.notes: Essentially the same as base PLA. Polymaker specifies 55 °C for 6 h for PolySonic PLA Pro and explicitly only 'if moisture absorbed'. Nothing in the nucleator/flow-modifier package is reported to change PLA's hygroscopicity, so the shorter, cooler drying regime of the base entry carries over — unlike pla-plus, where Bambu calls for a hotter 55-75 °C cycle.

storage.recommendations: Sealed bag or drybox with desiccant between uses; same tolerance for open-air storage in a dry room as base PLA

price.notes: Prusament PLA High Speed about $29.90/kg (1 kg spool, Prusa store, confirmed); eSUN ePLA-HS sits in the eSUN PLA+/Basic band at roughly $18-23/kg (unverified). A modest $5-10/kg premium over base PLA, the same tier as pla-plus and below pla-cf/lw-pla.

recommended: large draft models where print time dominates
not_recommended: parts where a matte, defect-hiding finish matters (glossier and less forgiving than matte PLA)
high-temperature parts (no thermal improvement over base PLA)
sustained-load structural parts (creep, as with base PLA)

properties.notes: Density is NOT published by Polymaker or Prusa for their high-speed grades; 1.24 g/cm³ is inherited from the base PLA entry on the basis that the chemistry is base polylactide plus nucleator/flow modifier (unverified for this grade specifically). Polymaker PolySonic PLA Pro: tensile X-Y 41.2±0.6 MPa at 'classic speed', bending strength X-Y 67.5±0.7 MPa, Charpy impact 22.7±2.5 kJ/m² — comparable to base PLA and sitting between base PLA and pla-plus on toughness, consistent with Polymaker's claim of 'impact strength similar to ABS'. The engineering delta of this grade is flow rate, not final part strength: Prusa's own figure is 28 mm³/s at 220 °C vs 24 mm³/s for standard Prusament PLA. Tg, HDT and shrinkage are not disclosed by any fetched source (unverified); expect base-PLA-like values around 55-60 °C since no chemistry change targets heat resistance, so no thermal numbers are recorded here rather than inventing them.

compatibility.notes: Same PLA-family bonding behaviour as the base entry: welds to itself and other PLA grades, does not weld to PETG/ABS/ASA/PC/PA/PP. Standard PLA-compatible breakaway or PVA/BVOH soluble supports. In multi-material jobs the tool-change and support-interface speeds are set by the slowest material, so the speed advantage is largely lost when co-printed with PVA.

plate_recommendations.notes: Same as base PLA — no release agent needed at 30-60 °C. Worth noting that first-layer adhesion is the limiting factor when the rest of the print runs at 250+ mm/s, so keep the first layer at normal PLA speeds.
Backfilled from plate entry (Phase E reciprocity): High-flow PLA is the material this plate is marketed alongside on the A1/P1/X1 high-speed profiles; behaviour matches base PLA.

emissions.notes: No unique emission concern beyond base PLA — no styrene, caprolactam or foaming agent. One practical caveat: ultrafine-particle emission scales with extruded mass per unit time, so a machine running this grade at 250-600 mm/s for hours puts out proportionally more than the same machine on a slow base-PLA profile, even though the per-gram emission profile is identical (inference, not a measured figure). Ventilate for continuous printing in an occupied room.

safety_notes: No food-contact certification found for any high-speed PLA line; brand-dependent and unverified, so treat as not food-safe.
additional_notes: Naming caveat for catalog mapping: Bambu Lab does not sell a filament literally called 'PLA-HF' — Bambu's 'HF' branding (as in PETG-HF) refers to the high-flow hotend/nozzle hardware, not to a PLA product. 'PLA-HF' in community usage maps to third-party high-speed PLA formulations (eSUN ePLA-HS, Polymaker PolySonic, Prusament PLA High Speed, colorFabb PLA High Speed Pro) run on fast printers. Realising the rated speed also needs the hardware: a high-flow hotend and strong part cooling, otherwise the grade behaves like ordinary PLA.

provenance.conflicts: Confidence is 'low' rather than 'medium' because the core physical data is missing: no fetched source publishes density, Tg, HDT or shrinkage for any high-speed PLA grade, so density is inherited from base PLA and thermal properties are omitted entirely. The speed ceiling also disagrees by source: Polymaker rates PolySonic PLA Pro at 100-300 mm/s while community and vendor marketing for the class cites 250-600+ mm/s — the range recorded spans both, but the upper end is hardware-dependent, not a material property. Naming is unresolved: 'PLA-HF' is a community label, not a manufacturer SKU, and Bambu's 'HF' means high-flow hardware rather than a filament grade.
